- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
  `install_local.sh`), and `site/install.sh.template` carries the same
  layout so regenerating the installers cannot resurrect the old one.
=======
- gh-1603: unattended runs can no longer end as a clean success on empty
  model responses. Loop: from the second empty-hiccup retry on, the request
  carries a continuation nudge user message ("your last reply was
  empty/truncated — continue the task"; exact-text constant
  `emptyContinuationNudge`, emitted with MessageStart/End so the transcript
  stays truthful) — a cap-truncated reasoning model re-streamed verbatim
  repeats the empty outcome, the nudge breaks the symmetry; the classifier
  treats that exact message as transparent, so the turn's partial-content
  window (gh-1577) survives a nudged retry. Headless: the empty-reply nudge
  budget rises to `AgentCliConfig.headlessEmptyReplyNudges` (default 2 — the
  session ends only after 3 consecutive unrecoverable empties; interactive
  keeps the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics), and a run that still settles
  empty prints the explicit `__FA_INCOMPLETE` marker and exits 1 — a
  distinguishable failure for the bench adapter, never a silent exit 0.

- gh-1577: an empty assistant completion after partial content (assistant
  text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is a
  bounded-retry provider hiccup — up to `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3)
  re-streams with exponential backoff (`emptyHiccupBaseDelay`,
  `emptyHiccupMaxBackoff`, both threaded through the `Agent` facade,
  `AgentWiringSpec`, and the CLI config), and exhaustion ends the run with
  a loud `StopReason.error` (headless exit 1, interactive error + prompt)
  instead of the silent exit-0 settle that killed the gh-1577 trials.
  Clean empties keep the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics. The abort always
  wins: a cancel racing the final retry settles `StopReason.aborted` for
  any empty shape (the exit-contract race is pinned by tests), and the

## Issues/Notes

- **Re-arm cause: merge conflict with `main`.** The silent branch update could not merge main; `merge_conflicts.md` flagged exactly one file with conflict markers: `CHANGELOG.md`. Everything else in the main sync auto-merged cleanly (staged, untouched).
- **The review findings were already fixed on this branch** (head `da7cb59e`, previous rework pass): the `/lib/` example path in `sqliteUnavailableMessage` (+ macOS fixture, CHANGELOG, PR description), the successor-side stale-layout repair `repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout()` (one `fa update` now heals on the first SQLite read), and loud lib-copy failures in both POSIX installers + `site/install.sh.template`. The three `PRRT_*` review threads carry the fix replies and are **resolved** — `pr_discussions.md` lists them under "3 resolved thread(s) excluded".
- The remaining `threads` entries in `pr_discussions_raw.json` (indexes 7/8/10) all have `threadId: null` and `rootCommentId: null`; two are machine records explicitly marked "Please do not edit or reply", and the third is the review **verdict** whose findings are the resolved `PRRT_*` threads above. There is no reply-able thread id among them — posting would produce untargeted top-level comments — so `outputs/review_replies.json` is `{ "replies": [] }`.

## Approach

1. Read all ticket/PR inputs; confirmed the only blocking item is the `CHANGELOG.md` conflict inside the in-progress `git merge origin/main`.
2. Resolved the conflict as a **union with the file's newest-first convention** (pinned by `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart`: exactly one `## Unreleased`, curated window newest-first): main's newer entries (`gh-1603`, `gh-1577`) first, then the branch's review-corrected `gh-1574` entry, then the common `gh-1556`.
3. Verified the resolution is a faithful union — each entry byte-identical to its source side (`diff` vs `da7cb59e:CHANGELOG.md` and `origin/main:CHANGELOG.md`), no conflict markers left, `git diff --check` clean.
4. Staged the resolved file (`git add CHANGELOG.md`) and left the merge **uncommitted** per `merge_conflicts.md` — the commit and push are handled automatically.
5. Verified the merged tree: targeted suites + scoped `dart analyze` green (see Test Coverage), full pre-merge scope suite in background.

## Files Modified

- `CHANGELOG.md` — conflict resolution only (no content authored: pure union of both parents' `## Unreleased` entries in the established newest-first order).
- No source files touched this pass; the PR's code (`sqlite_reader.dart`, `sqlite3_engine.dart`, `bin/self_manage.dart`, installers) is unchanged from the reviewed head `da7cb59e`.

## Test Coverage

- `test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` + `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` + `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart` on the resolved, staged merge tree: **109 passed** (CHANGELOG curation guard + the gh-1574 degradation/layout/repair/installer-contract suites).
- `dart analyze` on `lib/src/tools/sqlite`, `bin/self_manage.dart` and their tests: no issues.
- Full CI pre-merge scope (`dart test --exclude-tags integration,browser-ext`) on the staged tree: **10,573 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures** (background job `sh-11-hn7jsov9qfetyja1`, exit 0).

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in

blocks.text:
# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the clean note's example path is wrong (`~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` should be `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`)**

`sqliteUnavailableMessage` states the general rule correctly, then contradicts it in the same sentence:

```dart
'<exe_dir>/../lib — e.g. ~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib for '
'~/.local/bin/fa. ...'
```

For exe `~/.local/bin/fa`, `<exe_dir>/../lib` + name is `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib` — not `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib`. The ticket's real error text confirms the `/lib/` component: `Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`.

The no-`/lib` shape has propagated into four places and should be fixed in all of them:

1. this message (user-facing — a user told to "check `~/.local/libsqlite3.dylib`" will look in the wrong directory),
2. the macOS test fixture `_macMissingDylibError` in `test/tools/sqlite_engine_test.dart` (`/Users/someone/.local/libsqlite3.dylib`) — the Linux fixture in the same file has the correct `../lib/libsqlite3.so` shape,
3. the CHANGELOG entry (same mis-transcribed error quote),
4. the PR description's quoted error.

Classification itself is unaffected (both shapes match the `isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure` substrings), and the repair commands in the note are correct — but since this note is the deliverable of the ticket, the path in it should be the one the user actually needs to check.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: one `fa update` from a pre-fix binary does NOT heal the layout — the old binary runs its own baked-in (broken) copy code**

`copyBundleLibs` executes inside the *currently running* binary's process. A pre-fix binary's `fa update` therefore:

1. swaps in the fixed binary (good),
2. but then copies the bundle libs with the **old** code, back into `<installDir>/lib` (the broken layout).

The layout only heals on the **second** `fa update` (run by the fixed binary), or on a reinstall. This matters because the broken population this ticket serves is exactly the pre-fix installs — their repair path is: broken → `fa update` → still broken (now with the clean note) → `fa update` again → fixed.

Two concrete consequences:

- The PR description claim "Existing installs broken by the old layout heal on the next reinstall **or `fa update`**" overstates the update path; please correct it (and ideally the CHANGELOG wording) so the repair story is accurate.
- Consider making the note's advice robust for this window: either prefer "Reinstall fa" as the primary repair for old installs, or add a one-time successor-side layout repair (e.g. on boot, if `<exe_dir>/lib/<libsqlite3.*>` exists and `<exe_dir>/../lib/` does not, migrate it — the stale `bin/lib` leftovers are otherwise guaranteed to exist for every install made by the old installers).

No data-loss risk and the system converges either way — hence IMPORTANT, not blocking.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-13):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the lib copy still swallows failures silently (`2>/dev/null || true`)**

```sh
cp -r "$tmp_extract/bundle/lib/"* "$lib_dir/" 2>/dev/null || true
```

If this `cp` fails (permissions on a shared `~/.local/lib`, disk full, existing non-directory at the target), the installer still prints `ok "Installed $target"` and the user is left with exactly the gh-1574 symptom — previously undiscoverable, now at least reported by the new clean note. Since the whole point of this fix is "libs must land in `<exe_dir>/../lib`", a failed copy is no longer a cosmetic detail; consider letting it fail loudly (or printing a warning naming `$lib_dir`) instead of `|| true`. Same pattern in `install_local.sh` line 45.

Pre-existing style carried over, so suggestion-level — a good follow-up rather than a rework blocker.

blocks.text:
# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
  `install_local.sh`), and `site/install.sh.template` carries the same
  layout so regenerating the installers cannot resurrect the old one.
=======

  model responses. Loop: from the second empty-hiccup retry on, the request
  carries a continuation nudge user message ("your last reply was
  empty/truncated — continue the task"; exact-text constant
  `emptyContinuationNudge`, emitted with MessageStart/End so the transcript
  stays truthful) — a cap-truncated reasoning model re-streamed verbatim
  repeats the empty outcome, the nudge breaks the symmetry; the classifier
  treats that exact message as transparent, so the turn's partial-content
  window (gh-1577) survives a nudged retry. Headless: the empty-reply nudge
  budget rises to `AgentCliConfig.headlessEmptyReplyNudges` (default 2 — the
  session ends only after 3 consecutive unrecoverable empties; interactive
  keeps the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics), and a run that still settles
  empty prints the explicit `__FA_INCOMPLETE` marker and exits 1 — a
  distinguishable failure for the bench adapter, never a silent exit 0.

- gh-1577: an empty assistant completion after partial content (assistant
  text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is a
  bounded-retry provider hiccup — up to `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3)
  re-streams with exponential backoff (`emptyHiccupBaseDelay`,
  `emptyHiccupMaxBackoff`, both threaded through the `Agent` facade,
  `AgentWiringSpec`, and the CLI config), and exhaustion ends the run with

  instead of the silent exit-0 settle that killed the gh-1577 trials.
  Clean empties keep the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics. The abort always
  wins: a cancel racing the final retry settles `StopReason.aborted` for
  any empty shape (the exit-contract race is pinned by tests), and the

blocks.text:
# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
  `install_local.sh`), and `site/install.sh.template` carries the same
  layout so regenerating the installers cannot resurrect the old one.

blocks.text:
# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
  `install_local.sh`), and `site/install.sh.template` carries the same
  layout so regenerating the installers cannot resurrect the old one.
=======
- gh-1603: unattended runs can no longer end as a clean success on empty
  model responses. Loop: from the second empty-hiccup retry on, the request
  carries a continuation nudge user message ("your last reply was
  empty/truncated — continue the task"; exact-text constant
  `emptyContinuationNudge`, emitted with MessageStart/End so the transcript
  stays truthful) — a cap-truncated reasoning model re-streamed verbatim
  repeats the empty outcome, the nudge breaks the symmetry; the classifier
  treats that exact message as transparent, so the turn's partial-content
  window (gh-1577) survives a nudged retry. Headless: the empty-reply nudge
  budget rises to `AgentCliConfig.headlessEmptyReplyNudges` (default 2 — the
  session ends only after 3 consecutive unrecoverable empties; interactive
  keeps the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics), and a run that still settles
  empty prints the explicit `__FA_INCOMPLETE` marker and exits 1 — a
  distinguishable failure for the bench adapter, never a silent exit 0.

- gh-1577: an empty assistant completion after partial content (assistant
  text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is a
  bounded-retry provider hiccup — up to `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3)
  re-streams with exponential backoff (`emptyHiccupBaseDelay`,
  `emptyHiccupMaxBackoff`, both threaded through the `Agent` facade,
  `AgentWiringSpec`, and the CLI config), and exhaustion ends the run with
  a loud `StopReason.error` (headless exit 1, interactive error + prompt)
  instead of the silent exit-0 settle that killed the gh-1577 trials.
  Clean empties keep the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics. The abort always
  wins: a cancel racing the final retry settles `StopReason.aborted` for
  any empty shape (the exit-contract race is pinned by tests), and the

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

<<<<<<< HEAD
- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
  `install_local.sh`), and `site/install.sh.template` carries the same
  layout so regenerating the installers cannot resurrect the old one.
=======
- gh-1603: unattended runs can no longer end as a clean success on empty
  model responses. Loop: from the second empty-hiccup retry on, the request
  carries a continuation nudge user message ("your last reply was
  empty/truncated — continue the task"; exact-text constant
  `emptyContinuationNudge`, emitted with MessageStart/End so the transcript
  stays truthful) — a cap-truncated reasoning model re-streamed verbatim
  repeats the empty outcome, the nudge breaks the symmetry; the classifier
  treats that exact message as transparent, so the turn's partial-content
  window (gh-1577) survives a nudged retry. Headless: the empty-reply nudge
  budget rises to `AgentCliConfig.headlessEmptyReplyNudges` (default 2 — the
  session ends only after 3 consecutive unrecoverable empties; interactive
  keeps the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics), and a run that still settles
  empty prints the explicit `__FA_INCOMPLETE` marker and exits 1 — a
  distinguishable failure for the bench adapter, never a silent exit 0.

- gh-1577: an empty assistant completion after partial content (assistant
  text, tool activity, or a truncation signal earlier in the turn) is a
  bounded-retry provider hiccup — up to `emptyHiccupRetries` (default 3)
  re-streams with exponential backoff (`emptyHiccupBaseDelay`,
  `emptyHiccupMaxBackoff`, both threaded through the `Agent` facade,
  `AgentWiringSpec`, and the CLI config), and exhaustion ends the run with
  a loud `StopReason.error` (headless exit 1, interactive error + prompt)
  instead of the silent exit-0 settle that killed the gh-1577 trials.
  Clean empties keep the #1085 M2b one-nudge semantics. The abort always
  wins: a cancel racing the final retry settles `StopReason.aborted` for
  any empty shape (the exit-contract race is pinned by tests), and the
  backoff sleep is cancellation-aware.

# gh-1574: [BUG] read tool on .db/.sqlite fails: libsqlite3.dylib not found (installer puts it in bin/lib, binary looks in ../lib)

## Description

## Summary
The builtin `read` tool on a `.db/.sqlite` file fails on fa 1.0.565 (macOS arm64, installed in `~/.local/bin/fa`):

```
Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' ... Failed to load dynamic library '/Users/<user>/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib' (no such file)
```

## Reproduction
`read path=~/.fah/ledger.db` (any SQLite database).

## Cause
The binary resolves `../lib/libsqlite3.dylib` relative to `fa`, i.e. `~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`, but the installer places the bundle libs in `~/.local/bin/lib/` (`install_local.sh` and `bin/self_manage.dart` `_copyBundleLibs` both copy to `<installDir>/lib`). On this machine the dylib lives at `~/.local/bin/lib/libsqlite3.dylib`; it only worked because of a manual symlink at `~/.local/lib/`.

## Expected (either)
- Install the dylib where the binary looks (`<installDir>/../lib`), or make the binary look in `<installDir>/lib` too; and/or
- Fall back to the system library (`/usr/lib/libsqlite3.dylib` on macOS, `libsqlite3.so.0` on Linux) when the bundled one is missing.
- A missing library must produce a clean "sqlite unavailable" note, as the tool does when no engine is wired, rather than a raw FFI error.

## Tests
Installer layout test (dylib reachable from the binary's lookup path) and an engine-loader test with a missing bundled lib falling back / degrading cleanly.

  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
  `install_local.sh`), and `site/install.sh.template` carries the same
  layout so regenerating the installers cannot resurrect the old one.

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in

- gh-1574: SQLite reads work on installed binaries — bundle libs land where
  the binary looks. The AOT binary's native-assets resolver reads
  `<exe_dir>/../lib/<name>` (the `dart build cli` bundle layout), but every
  POSIX installer copied the bundle libs beside the binary
  (`<install_dir>/lib`), so `read path=x.db` died with a raw FFI dump
  (`Couldn't resolve native function 'sqlite3_initialize' … Failed to load
  dynamic library '~/.local/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'`); it only worked on machines
  with a manual symlink in `~/.local/lib`. Fixed the layout in all three
  install paths — `site/install.sh` (incl. the quarantine-xattr pass and the
  source-build advice), `install_local.sh`, and `fa update`
  (`bin/self_manage.dart` `copyBundleLibs`, now public and layout-pinned by
  tests; also aligns Windows `fa update` with `install.ps1`, which was
  already correct) — plus clean degradation in the FFI engine:
  `Sqlite3Engine.openReadOnly` classifies the dart:ffi resolver's
  library-load failure (`isSqliteDynamicLibraryLoadFailure`) and throws a
  clean `SQLite is unavailable — reinstall or run fa update` note instead of
  the raw resolver dump; a Dart-level system-library fallback is impossible
  with package:sqlite3 native assets (build-time asset mapping, no loader
  override). Installs already broken by the old layout self-heal: on the
  bundled library's first failed load the binary moves the stale
  `<exe_dir>/libsqlite3.*` into `<exe_dir>/../lib/` and retries the load
  (`repairStaleSqliteBundleLayout`) — so one `fa update` suffices (the
  successor binary repairs on its first SQLite read; a pre-fix binary cannot
  repair itself), and the stale `<bin>/lib` leftovers disappear as they
  migrate. The POSIX installers also report a failed lib copy instead of
  swallowing it (`site/install.sh` warns naming the lib dir; same in
